what: Holistic recall design (finalized): Four scopes, four mechanisms. (1) SESSION-SCOPED: SessionStart auto-injects top 15 most-recalled preferences + all guidelines, capped ~300 tokens. Memories can have priority: "always" (user-marked, always injected) or "normal" (subject to cap). Scope-specific preferences still surfaced via path hooks. (2) PATH-SCOPED: Read/Edit hooks show ALL four layer counts in preview, not just technical/area_context. Separate file|path and dir|path tracking entries. File recall on first read, directory recall forced on 2nd file in same dir. (3) QUERY-SCOPED: Grep/Glob hook runs keyword search preview (~80ms latency, imperceptible). Blocks if matches>0. (4) CORRECTION-SCOPED: UserPromptSubmit soft + flag, Stop checks flag. Deduplication: track returned memory IDs in session file (ids|5,11,15...), aide_recall filters out already-returned IDs. Zero duplicate tokens across file + directory recalls.
why: Stress-tested across 8 scenarios. Key findings: keyword search is ~80ms (fast enough for hook), SessionStart injection needs a cap (~15 preferences), file+directory need separate tracking with ID-based deduplication to avoid duplicate tokens.
